'''Fan Haifu''' ({{zh|c=范海福|p=Fàn Haǐfú}}; 15 August 1933 – 8 July 2022)<ref>[http://news.bandao.cn/a/640308.html 晶体学家范海福院士逝世] {{in lang|zh}}</ref> was a Chinese crystallographer, physicist, and writer. He was a member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and [[TWAS|The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cryst.iphy.ac.cn/FANHF/fanhf_e.html |title=Prof. Fan, Hai-fu }}</ref>

==Biography==
Fan was born and raised in [[Guangzhou]], [[Guangdong]], during the [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]]. He secondary studied at Guangdong Experimental High School ({{zh|s=广东实验中学|links=no}}).<ref name="man">{{cite news|url=https://www.cas.cn/xw/cmsm/201210/t20121008_3655464.shtml |title=【中国科学报】范海福："偶然"造就科学人生 |newspaper=Chinese Academy of Sciences |date=8 October 2012 |language= zh}}</ref> He graduated from [[Peking University]] in 1956, where he majored in chemistry. He studied chemistry and physics under Tang Youqi ({{zh|s=唐有祺|links=no}}), Fu Ying ({{zh|s=傅鹰|links=no}}), [[Xu Guangxian]], [[Zhou Guangzhao]], Chen Shaoli ({{zh|s=陈绍礼|links=no}}), and Wu Qianzhang ({{zh|s=吴乾章|links=no}}).<ref name="man"/> After graduation, he applied for an internship in the Institute of Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and became a professor at [[University of Science and Technology of China]] and [[Sun Yat-sen University]].

He was elected a fellow of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1991 and a fellow of [[TWAS|the World Academy of Sciences]] in 2000. He is also a recipient of the 1996 [[TWAS Prize]].<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |url=https://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards |title=Prizes and Awards |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fan married [[Li Fanghua]], who was also a Chinese physicist.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.beijingreview.com.cn/2009news/guonei/keji/2010-03/17/content_255250.htm |title=李方华：科学对性别无偏见 |newspaper=Beijing REviews |date= 17 March 2010 |language= zh}}</ref>

==Book==
* ''Physical and Non-Physical Methods of Solving Crystal Structures''  (collaboration with [[Michael Woolfson]])

==Awards==
*The Second Class Prize of Natural Sciences of China (1987)
*The TWAS award in physics (1996)
*The Tan Kah Kee Science Award in mathematics and physics (2006)
